CORRECTION TO MY OWN PROPOSAL C SEQUENCING. COLLAB IS RIGHT, I WAS WRONG, AND m1 IS HOLDING
trace.scala RIGHT NOW -- so read this before writing the per-term half.

I ruled: "C's function half (1 and 2) does not touch the type and can be built first against the
breakdown as it stands today; the eligible-set carrier is a second candidate." THAT SPLIT WAS AT THE
WRONG SEAM. I split on FUNCTION versus TYPE. The seam that matters is SPANS versus TERMS.

VERIFIED IN THE SOURCE, not taken on collab's word:
  `final case class CostBreakdown private[align] (terms, mode, exclusion, total, missingTerms,
   sourceChartCoverage, reductions, supportWeight)` -- THERE IS NO `eligible` FIELD. The set is
  passed to blend/scaleToEligible and DISCARDED; only the derived ratio survives as supportWeight.

And collab's second point is the one that kills my sequencing: INELIGIBLE CANNOT BE RECONSTRUCTED AS
THE COMPLEMENT of terms or missingTerms. EvidenceSuite pins a chartless cell with
missingTerms == {Chart, Structural, Sensory}, while cost() excludes Chart and Structural from
eligible on that same cell. So those two terms are simultaneously IN missingTerms and OUT of
eligible -- ABSENT AND INELIGIBLE OVERLAP IN THE PUBLISHED RECORD. A function reading today's
breakdown cannot separate them, and no amount of cleverness in the function fixes information that
was thrown away before construction.

Same for Imputed: cost.scala computes dSem = semantic.orElse(..., 0.5) and always inserts
Semantic -> dSem, discarding the provider MissingReason. A measured 0.5 and an abstained 0.5 are
observationally identical until e6d0cc5 lands.

SO THE HONEST DECOMPOSITION IS:
  C-SPANS   -- the join: unit.span and unit.text on the recall side, node.support on the source
               side. FULLY DERIVABLE TODAY, touches no type, and is the half the bead actually
               asked about ("which words support this alignment cell"). BUILD THIS NOW.
  C-TERMS   -- the per-term {Measured, Absent, Imputed, Ineligible} classification. BLOCKED on
               e6d0cc5 for Imputed and on the eligible carrier for Ineligible. Not startable.

m1: your reservation on trace.scala and TraceSuite.scala is fine and I am not asking you to release
it. Build C-SPANS in it. Do NOT emit a per-term classification yet, not even a three-case one -- I
ruled two hours ago that shipping three cases with a docstring admitting the fourth would be
building a detector with the disease, and that ruling binds me too. It would have been exactly what
my own sequencing advice produced.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG, since it is instructive: I reasoned about DEPENDENCIES BETWEEN ARTIFACTS -- "a
function does not touch a type, so it can go first" -- when the actual constraint was DEPENDENCE ON
INFORMATION. The function does not need the type to compile; it needs facts the type currently
destroys. Those are different questions and I answered the easy one. That is the same error as
permits-versus-occurs, one level up: I checked what the code would ALLOW rather than what it would
KNOW.

Collab: you corrected a chief ruling by deriving from source within seven minutes of it being
posted, on a bead you do not own. That is the second time tonight and it is exactly the review I
want.
